**GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD - General Certificate of Education Examination. JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL. English Language, Paper 2 (0730).**

Answer your questions either exclusively from **PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS)** or from **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS)**.

**PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS) - Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours.** Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION (Section A: Composition, Section B: Prescribed Texts, Section C: Creative Writing). ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - Duration: Three Hours.** Instructions to candidates: Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.

questions.enonce_markdown: **3.** Using any three prescribed texts, justify the assertion that writers of the prescribed texts have different views about love.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method answer: the prescribed texts are not available here, so no detail of any work is given. Apply this method to the three texts you have studied.**

**Understanding the question**

- 'love': it can be romantic love between a man and a woman, but also love of family, of a child, of friends, of the community or of the homeland.
- 'different views': the writers do not treat love in the same way: it may be a source of joy and strength, a cause of pain or betrayal, a duty and sacrifice, a bond that money or tradition can destroy, or something to be mocked.
- 'justify': defend the assertion with evidence from exactly three texts, showing a real difference of view between them.

**Plan**

1. Introduction: name three texts and writers, say that love is a common subject but treated differently, and announce the views you will show.
2. Body, organised by VIEW (not text by text), or text by text if you end with a comparison: for each view, who holds it, how the writer presents it (action, speech, imagery, outcome) and one precise detail or short quotation.
3. A paragraph that compares the three views and explains the difference (different contexts, characters, purposes, tone).
4. Conclusion: what the differences show about love and about the writers.

**Ideas to test against your own texts (suggestions only, to be checked)**: love as sacrifice, love as selfish possession, love that survives hardship, love betrayed, love of country, love tied to money or tradition.

**Opening pattern**: 'Love is a theme that the writers of the prescribed texts all explore, but they do not share one view of it. In [Text A] it is..., in [Text B]... while in [Text C]...'

**Marking grid (indicative; the paper prints only 20 marks)**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Relevance and argument | A clear thesis that answers the question, kept up to the end |
| Knowledge of the texts | Accurate, precise evidence (event, character, short quotation) from exactly three texts |
| Organisation | Introduction, well-ordered paragraphs, conclusion |
| Expression and accuracy | Formal register, linking words, correct grammar and spelling |

**Common mistakes**

1. Describing every love story without showing a difference of view.
2. Only one kind of love (romantic) in all three texts: choose texts and examples that really differ.
3. Missing the word 'different': the answer must compare the writers' views, not only list the examples.
